target.title: improve: skill auto-capture catches reactive corrections and routes them to existing skills
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Autonomous skill capture (`skills.workshop.autonomous.enabled`) misses most real feedback. Field evidence from a live two-day agent deployment: a user gave ~a dozen durable corrections ("that's not what I asked", "you're still using the coach transcripts", "I thought we were working on listening", "I don't wanna have to repeat myself") and **zero** were captured, because:
- the signal patterns only match prospective phrasing ("from now on", "remember to") — never reactive corrections, which dominate real sessions;
- only the single last matching instruction per session survives (`findLast`);
- topic routing is hard-coded to four dev topics, so domain corrections pile into a generic `learned-workflows` skill instead of updating the skill they're about;
- failed runs skip capture entirely — yet a correction given right before a timeout is exactly the one worth keeping (this happened: a 600s CLI timeout ate the session's most important correction).

## Why This Change Was Made
Capture both signal shapes (prospective + a conservative reactive set), sweep up to 8 instructions per session grouped into ≤3 proposals by target skill, and route each group to the existing workspace skill it is about via name/description vocabulary overlap — using a new `listWritableWorkspaceSkillSummaries` helper built on the same `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` discovery `proposeUpdateSkill` uses, so routing only ever lands on skills an update proposal can actually write (`openclaw-workspace` and `agents-skills-project` sources, including `.agents/skills`). The create-vs-update branch reads the matched skill's real file path instead of assuming the flat layout. Capture now also runs on failed turns: the extracted signals are the user's own words, which stay valid when the run dies.

Everything stays inside the existing safety envelope: feature remains opt-in (`autonomous.enabled: false` default), proposals stay `pending` behind the security scan + human approval, per-skill dedup against pending/quarantined proposals is unchanged, and skill reads go through the symlink/hardlink-rejecting safe reader.

## User Impact
Users who enable autonomous capture stop repeating themselves: reactive corrections become pending workshop proposals targeted at the right skill (e.g. a correction about a `signal-scout` workspace skill becomes an update proposal for that skill, not a new generic one), several distinct corrections in one long session all survive, and feedback given in a turn that later fails/times out is no longer lost. Docs updated (`docs/tools/skill-workshop.md`).

## Evidence
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/ src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts src/agents/harness/` → 208 passed (10 files, 3 shards), including new coverage: reactive-pattern capture/ignore matrix, per-topic grouping, recency-correct proposal cap, existing-skill routing (flat `skills/` and `.agents/skills` project skill, with apply-through verification), failed-run capture, multi-proposal sessions.
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in touched modules.
- `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` (codex/gpt-5.5): **clean — no accepted/actionable findings; overall: patch is correct (0.86)**. Three earlier findings were fixed in-branch (safe-reader reuse for the summary scan; recency-correct cap via group re-insertion; writable-source routing via the workshop service helper).

Origin: gaps found while auditing a live OpenClaw agent ("Loom") content-engine deployment where user feedback repeatedly failed to reach skills.
